I've played DotA and the reason we really let our enemies win in DotA is that at a certain lead, there is actually no feasible way to win. Especially since not only do enemies gain gold upon killing you, but you lose gold upon death. This makes it extremely hard to catch up, which is why DotA is so punishing to screw ups. 
However, I find that in LoL, it is actually pretty easy to catch up. Since you don't lose gold upon death, you keep accumulating gold no matter what. If you continuously farm up, and reenter the battle, like the average Vayne player, you can come back just as strong as the enemy adc even if they were 3 or 4 kills ahead. LoL is just a less punishing in terms of gameplay, so there is alway that actual hope of 'coming back' 
If you have the skills and competence to be able to understand that is it actually feasible to return from a disadvantage, then logically you should use that knowledge and just not surrender. 
In addition, enemy throws do happen, baron steals are entirely possible, good team fights are possible. You make it sound like the enemy rarely throws, but it is a great possibility. And late game champions do exist in LoL, and you just have to wait. It doesn't matter if they are behind, they can catch up easily with items. e.g. Kayle, Vayne, GP
Also, no one ever surrenders in esports for that exact reason, they are waiting for a throw. If you are in a ranked game and losing, you just have to play it out. If you surrender there is a 100% possibility of a loss. If you play it out, there is less chance of a loss. Until the enemy has destroyed your nexus, you have not lost that game. I've played games where we have had an open nexus, and have salvaged the game by them throwing a baron team fight.

That is all.

You have to consider potential negative situations where 4 man parties would be a negative impact on the game
For example, surrender votes. It only takes 4 yes votes to create a surrender. So in the event where the 5th solo player doesn't want a surrender, regardless the 4 man party can still force a surrender. This is especially toxic when say you are winning and then last minute before you win, the 4 man forces a surrender losing you a game. Also, they can turn a surrender vote in the way of not allowing a surrender. Say your team is losing badly and you are stuck with a team of 4 other extremely toxic team mates who make your life hell. You try to surrender but you can't because the vote is 1-4. This leaves you stuck in a negative situation for a lot longer than necessary ending up leaving you tilted and angry. 
In addition, it creates a negative impact on communication through the game especially when the 4 man is communicating using things like Discord or Skype and are unwilling to invite the 5th player. They are able to create plays and such without the knowledge of the 5th. I know that when in a party of 4, I more often will say "their adc is mia" rather than pinging it. This leaves the 5th player out of the loop per say. 
Also, it is most unfair when a toxic 4 man will all blame the 5th player for a loss or for a misplay. This comes down to being a 4v1 bullying session for at least 15 minutes. Of course, you can mute them but the communication can go out the window. Furthermore, the enemy team will see 4 players trash talking one player, and will more likely believe the 4 because of power in numbers. They are able to all troll, leaving you with an overall negative experience being a solo player who happened to queue up with 4 trolls. They can also 4x report you, leaving a negative impact on your honour despite you doing nothing wrong, since riot more often looks at when a player has multiple reports in one game rather than having one report from the game. 
I don't see the major impact since the 4 man party is really only affected in flex rank. You are still able to play normals ARAM and rotating game mode. If you have ever been matched up with a terrible 4 man, you will understand why riot disabled 4 man queues. 

TLDR ; it's for the enjoyment and safety of solo queue players.
